Who would have thought when I boarded a plane for Greece more than 20 years ago, planning on backpacking through the mountains and then heading north through then Yugoslavia I'd end up making Greece my second home?
But here I am, 20 something years later, with our fabulous biz "Greek Vacation Rentals",  opening up our amazing Acropolis view family & group friendly Athens apartments & our MagicFactoryLofts, spacious art filled homes in Chicago, while planning RealGreece travel itineraries and leading small group food & wine focused tours around my adopted homeland and loving the life that I am lucky enough to be living. Of course I did pick up an equally crazy, workaholic Greek husband along the way, as well as a stray Greek animal or two!

Update: January 2023 .... This year Basil and I celebrate 20 years opening our Greek vacation rentals to guests from around the world. All these years we've been hopping between Basil's home city, Athens and Carole's home city of Chicago.  Time and time again guests in Greece asked us if they can stay in our Chicago home while we're in Athens.... so now you can stay in Chicago in our art filled Magic Factory Lofts. We've got 3 and 4 bedroom homes in the heart of the city with Big Shoulders -  in our hybrid warehouse (which in a previous life housed a bar and a dance hall, followed by a costume and magic card factory and then a photography studio where probably every Butterball turkey advertisement in the 1980s was shot .... the photos, not the turkeys!)

So come stay with us ... and then stay with us again. Whether you'd like to enjoy an ouzo in Athens overlooking the Acropolis the Acropolis View Alpha or 7 bedroom  Acropolis SkyVilla, or a beer and a hot dog in Chicago while staying at  our Magic Factory Lofts  we know that you won't be disappointed. 

All of our places are perfect for 3 generation families, multiple couples (especially in Athens pre or post cruise), or groups of friends on a city break or vacation.

name: Full Flat 150m2 Victoria Square Cntl Ath. 1’@metro
description: Spacious, (150 square meters) simply decorated with tall ceilings, on the first floor of a neoclassical building. Right in front of Victoria train station, it is a short walk to the park, cinema, bars etc. You will enjoy returning to the serene atmosphere of this home after a long day out.
neighborhood_overview:
Off the beaten track but located down-town, Victoria square with its renowned train station is Athens’ most multicultural area. Adjacent to the court houses and Kypseli, a work commuting and meeting area. Plenty of necessary shops, cinema and a big park. Originally an upper district of Athens, central to theatres and social life. Gradually the demographics changed and in recent years, artists, creatives and students have moved in bridging a wave with pop-up galleries, studios or the occasional art installation or peaceful protest on the square. Have a drink at 'Match Point' (Woody Allen fans) across the flat on a pedestrian street. Grab a fresh fruit juice and walk over to the park or the Archaeological Museum then on to the Acropolis.
This area is for those that want to explore the raw and creative side of Athens from all walks of life. This area is linked to all places because it is so central.

It is a private home that utilises to support the building's maintenance and heritage. Occasionally let out for commercials, fashion shoots, film and art residencies.

Metaxourgeio is frequently described as a transition neighbourhood. After a long period of abandonment in the late 20th century, the area is acquiring a reputation as an artistic and fashionable neighbourhood due to the opening of many art galleries, museums, and trendy restaurants and cafes. Moreover, local efforts to beautify and invigorate the neighbourhood have reinforced a budding sense of community and artistic expression. description:

neighborhood_overview:
Psirri is a very special neighborhood.
In the beginning of the century, poor families from the aegean islands used to come here for work and built small houses. There is still a community of Naxos' people with small restaurants with live music and their traditional products such as cheese, seafood and goat's meat.
Another community of Psirri were the leather workers, making shoes and leather accessories, so there are still many manufacturers where you can buy or even order your own leather goods. These people worked in big industrial buildings built in Psirri during the '60s and '70s.
And last but most importantly, Psirri is surrounded by archeological sites The Acropolis, the Ancient Agora, the Cemetery of Keramikos. All in 3-10 minutes walk.
So, there is not only one way to describe Psirri. The diversity of it's character is what makes it so special and interesting.

Located conveniently in one of the safest neighborhoods, close to all the major attractions, just 5 mins from the metro station Megaro Moussikis & 2 stops away from the city centre. Ideal for a carefree & relaxing stay!
neighborhood_overview:
Mavili square neighborhood is an upmarket and trendy inner-city suburb – a small but buzzing area, especially in the evenings with al fresco dining spots and a couple of cosy local bars, including lesser-known underground places.

Supermarkets (including a 24/7), pharmacies and banks just around the corner. In Mavili Square (just 2 minutes from the house) there are restaurants, 24h kiosks, coffee shops and bars.

The Athens Concert Hall (Megaron Mousikis) that attracts a hip crowd. The Athens Concert Hall programme features Sunday Morning Events and an annual series of lectures delivered by renowned architects, writers and other individuals, for which admission is free. Behind that, you have a beautiful park and the highest hill in Athens to conquer – Lycabettus Hill.
host_about: A born and raised Athenian, went to London after graduating from high school to study Architecture and lived there for 5 years more or less before returning to my homeland. Seems like I'm kind of a restless soul; can't settle in one place for too long. I have lived in the UK, in Spain and I'm currently residing in Portugal. During all these years I found myself working on various projects, including a managerial position in a boutique hotel on the beautiful Greek island of Spetses. This experience taught me a lot and showed me how much I cherish hospitality and meeting new people. I also love everything creative, I've got a passion for arts n' crafts and interior design. In my free time I enjoy long walks with my dog in nature, good food, watching movies, reading books and playing games. My aspiration in life is to keep learning new cultures while traveling. Looking forward to welcoming you to Athens!

host_about:
Hi everyone. I am Stratos Zafeiriadis

I am a husband, a father of a 3yrs old child, a host, an Airbnb Community Leader in the capital of Greece, an Experience maker and a property manager in Greece (“where else” lol).

Stratos Zafeiriadis

host_about:
As you set out for Ithaka
hope the voyage is a long one,
full of adventure, full of discovery.
Laistrygonians and Cyclops,
angry Poseidon—don’t be afraid of them:
you’ll never find things like that on your way
as long as you keep your thoughts raised high,
as long as a rare excitement
stirs your spirit and your body.
Laistrygonians and Cyclops,
wild Poseidon—you won’t encounter them
unless you bring them along inside your soul,
unless your soul sets them up in front of you.
 
Hope the voyage is a long one.
May there be many a summer morning when,
with what pleasure, what joy,
you come into harbors seen for the first time;
may you stop at Phoenician trading stations
to buy fine things,
mother of pearl and coral, amber and ebony,
sensual perfume of every kind—
as many sensual perfumes as you can;
and may you visit many Egyptian cities
to gather stores of knowledge from their scholars.
 
Keep Ithaka always in your mind.
Arriving there is what you are destined for.
But do not hurry the journey at all.
Better if it lasts for years,
so you are old by the time you reach the island,
wealthy with all you have gained on the way,
not expecting Ithaka to make you rich.
 
Ithaka gave you the marvelous journey.
Without her you would not have set out.
She has nothing left to give you now.
 
And if you find her poor, Ithaka won’t have fooled you.
Wise as you will have become, so full of experience,
you will have understood by then what these Ithakas mean. 

Ithaka-C. P. Cavafy (greek poetry)

I wish you a wonderful stay!

Best,

Athina

Stay in the heart of PLAKA, just steps from the ACROPOLIS, in a bright, design-forward home, nestled in charming Anafiotika. neighborhood_overview:
The neighbourhood is called "Anafiotika" and it's the oldest and most famous district of Greece. If you've ever been at a Greek island and liked it, you'll love Anafiotika, a small "island" in the heart of Athens. A small search around the web will convince you!

Anafiotika, clinging to the north slope of the Acropolis, is a beautiful, architecturally distinct subdistrict of Plaka. In the mid-1800s, King Otto hired builders from Anafi to build a new palace. In their homes here, they mimicked their island's architecture, all whitewashed cubes, bedecked with bougainvillea and geraniums. The area now is a clutch of about 40 homes, linked by footpaths just wide enough for people and stray cats.

neighborhood_overview: Thiseio or Thissio (Greek: Θησείο) is the name of a traditional neighborhood in downtown Athens, Greece, northwest of the Acropolis, 1.5 km southwest of downtown. Long ago, the name was derived from the Temple of Hephaestus. The area has many cafés and cultural meeting points. Thissio is surrounded by hills, heights and historical sites which are within a walking distance. The Ancient Agora of Athens, Stoa of Attalos, the Temple of Hephaestus and Kerameikos Archaeological Museum can be entered from Thissio. All others: the National Observatory of Athens, Acropolis of Athens, Philopappos Monument, Mouseion Hill, Pnyx, which is considered the birthplace of Democracy and the Mount Lycabettus can be easily reached or viewed from Thiseio. The panoramic views of them and their natural surroundings from the Areopagus height are spectacular, especially by night.

My apartment is located at the foot of Acropolis Hill, walking distance to all ancient sights, parks, art and culture, great views, restaurants and dining spots. You’ll love the place because of the neighbourhood, the coziness, the comfy bed, and the kitchen.
We have an amazing rooftop veranda for your use, as you can see in the pictures, with spectacular views of the city and Acropolis.
neighborhood_overview: You are in the middle of most tourist and sightseeing action of Athens, in a vibrant central neighbourhood. You can walk to all sights in Athens by foot.
host_about:
My name is Eftihia (Eftehea), from the words 'ef' and 'tihi' (tehe) which mean 'good' and 'luck' in ancient greek. My name is also a noun. In modern greek the word eftihia means happiness. For ancient greeks happy was the fortunate one. Nowdays happy is the joyful one. My name is quite a heavy thing to go by everyday, as it means something so great and simple (but veeeery complicated too..), that it is sometimes a real struggle to deliver its meaning and idea and project in in your life. And other's lives around you.

My parents origins are from the Peloponese and Zakynthos (Ionian Island). But I grew up in the wider terretory of Attica Prefecture, in particular in 2 suberbs of Athens- Marousi and Kifisia.

My profession is acting and as that started as a career (B.C. - before Crisis!!!) but has practically ended up a practical hobby (A.C.- after Crisis..), I am trying to reinvent myself and my life and scetch a 'plan B'..

Whatever that will occur to be, my true passion is walking barefoot on sharp rocks of isolated greek islands. If I was from India I think they would say I used to be a wild goat in a previous life. My technique in this strange extreme sport is really something to admire. I love walking in general, I like nature and even though I am definately a child of the city, my soul meets its 'core' when away from it. It is like the purity of my existence absolutely relates to the inviroment I find myself in. The landscape of a mountain or a beach or a lake or a river automatically turns me into a better person. My effort has always been to manage to carry that person with me even in the packed and trafficy Streets and Avenues of Athens.

My favourite time of the day in the area I leave in (where my house that welcomes airbnb guests is located) is between 2-6 in the morning. When the city sleeps one is able to 'pick up' and fully absorb this area's true energy. When crowded it is just another touristic place with great historical interest. But its healing effect one can only get when it is  q u i t e  and  p e a c e f u l.. At times of grief, pressure or distress I found that walking (AND jogging too!) around in that neighbourhood at these hours of the day was very therapeutic.

Sharing your house with people you don't know (and- at circummstances- you might actually never even meet!!!) became possible thanks to this whole airbnb notion that you created. It is a beautiful chain that connects people who wanted more- out of traveling- than a regular hotel or rudimantary furnished/equipped apartments. That chain allows travellers to make a 'subtour'  in their tour, experience how a person from a different country and culture lives. Like a quick whimsy eavesdropping or innocent peeping that might 'salt or sweeten up' the first and last moments of ones journey to a foreign place. 

So.. Long live the AirBnB!

As one of the capital's leading shopping areas, it is also a fashionable meeting point and includes a variety of designer shops. One of its main shopping streets, Voukourestiou Street, is now known for its extensive jewelry collection. The Athens Concert Hall, a modern building which superb acoustics and facilities, the center of cultural musical life in Athens, is also located in the neighborhood. Museums and galleries also abound in the area with The Benaki Museum - inside a preserved neoclassical manor house - and the Goulandris Museum of Cycladic Art, as two of its finest examples. A walk across the street from Vasilissis Sofias Avenue will lead you to the Byzantine Museum, and the War Museum.

The district is named after Ioannis Makrygiannis, Greek general of the Greek War of Independence, who used to own a house and fields in the area. Opposite the house of Ioannis Makrygiannis a military hospital was built – known as Weiler Building after the architect who designed it.This building was later used as gendarmerie headquarters and a violent battle took place there during the Greek civil war, in 1944. In the Makrygianni's neighbourhood is located the new Acropolis Museum that was inaugurated in 2009. Makrygianni is a densely populated area - already congested by the 1960s and 1970s - but remains a relatively expensive neighborhood due to its proximity to the Acropolis ruins.

neighborhood_overview:
The Monastiraki and Psirri neighborhood is a commercial center during the day but is transformed to a popular nightspot during the evening.
The cosmopolitanism of the city is evident as locals, tourists and immigrants all intermingle in the vicinity.
Miaouli Street is primarily a trading place for leather and footwear items during the day, with various cafes and small restaurants providing an outlook to the local commercial activities. From the early afternoon, however, the cafes, restaurants, and bars attract a wide variety of people who want to smoke nargileh (oriental tobacco pipe), eat mezze (selection of small dishes) and drink tsipouro or have a drink and dance at the bars. Finally, in recent years Athens has become a sort of graffiti Mecca and the neighborhood is one of the main areas in Athens where one can observe the transformation of old or abandoned buildings by young street artists.
host_about:

I returned to Athens just when the financial crisis struck hard and I have found myself being involved in the Miaouli8 project. Miaouli8 is a collection of lofts and spaces situated in an industrial building built by my grandfather in the mid 1960s.
The listings that I am hosting are the outcome of an inventive effort to revive the unused spaces of the building. Using old family furniture, second hand vintage objects from flea markets and a lot of personal work, we have transformed these former craft spaces into modern Athenian apartments.

Images of crowds on Evripidou Street are nothing new. Ever since 1886, the year the city’s municipal market opened its doors, the Ermou-Stadiou-Athinas street triangle along with the broader Monastiraki area have maintained close links with the food trade. The portion of Evripidou stretching from Aeolou to Menandrou streets, for instance, hosts 15 spice and 12 food stores. In between these are artisan’s shops selling equipment (barrels, sacks) for the distribution of the market’s wares. How these highly specialized stores selling everything from lamp hats to zippers, baskets, corks, essential oils, sieves and fishing and hunting gear survive is a mystery. neighborhood_overview:
Location
Tripodon street is considered as the oldest street of Athens. It is located in the same place as it was 25 centuries ago and has the same name since then.

The Way of Glory
The very precious story of Tripodon Street begins from the fact that it was, perhaps, the broadest street of ancient Athens (six meters wide) and the shortest one to go from the theater of Dionysus to the Agora. It was not done to serve the city's traffic, but to get the Athenians to watch the theatrical performances of Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides and Aristophanes. It was the street of Art, the Philosophers, the Theater, the Architecture, the Greek Thought. In this way the torch relaying took place in honor of the god Dionysus.

It is here that the Athens Polytechnic uprising of November 1973 took place.
Exarcheia is a place where many intellectuals and artists live.

name: Parthenon View:Acropolis Neoclassical Apt &Terrace
description: This lovely, fully renovated two bedroom and two bathroom neoclassical apartment is on the first floor (second floor in the U.S.) of our elegant Athenian home located on a quiet street 200 meters from the foot of the Acropolis. From their private split-level roof garden terrace guests enjoy rare and stunning up-close views of the Acropolis and of the Parthenon temple itself.
neighborhood_overview:
Our home is in the heart of a quiet but vibrant neighborhood. While removed from the tourist crowds, we have immediate access (five to ten minutes by foot) to the Acropolis and the Acropolis Museum as well as the popular Plaka and Thissio quarters. Steps away are the Hill of the Muses (Philopappou Hill) for taking walks with spectacular views of Athens and the sea, and the ancient Herodion Theatre (Odeon of Herodes Atticus) where performances of theatre, dance and music take place during the summer months and through mid-October.

The surrounding streets and squares of Koukaki and Makriyianni are brimming with restaurants, cafés and bars. For guests’ daily needs there are grocery stores and pharmacies within a five-minute walk, as well as one of Athens’ most famous bakeries. Fresh fruits and vegetables and other local products are available in abundance at our weekly outdoor farmers’ market (a ten to fifteen minute walk depending on the season).
host_about: Our family of four includes two generations and two cultures and is engaged in multiple ways in the literary, artistic, educational and culinary life of Greece. We are excited about meeting and hosting guests who will enjoy and appreciate our house and city to their fullest, and we look forward to making them feel at home in both!

Extract from ''Lonely Planet''
Kolonaki is an adjective as much as a district: it best epitomises the Athenian elite. Undeniably chic, Kolonaki is where old money mixes with the nouveau-riche and wannabes. Named after a tiny obscure column in the central Plateia Kolonakiou (Kolonaki Sq), Kolonaki stretches from Syntagma to the foothills of Lykavittos Hill, and is home to consistently popular cafes, restaurants, galleries, museums, boutiques and stylish apartment blocks. The area also contains a couple of notable museums and cultural institutions, which add to the air of nobility. The leafy upper reaches of Kolonaki transition into Lykavittos Hill, the highest point in central Athens. The wooden amphitheater up here hosts regular concerts during the summer.

neighborhood_overview:
Kerameikos/Gazi is the new 'Soho' of Athens, with most major historical sites located within a 25-minute walking radius. It is safe, urban and lively, full of
unique shops, authentic tavernas, cafes, art galleries and so-far remains un-touristic. Strolling through Kerameikos in the daytime can also be deceptively low-key. During the day many Greeks go about their day, but at night the many local bars, taverns and hotspots fill up with mainly an artistic crowd from the surrounding areas. There is a supermarket and deli at just 100 meters from the house, with fresh and organic fruits and vegetables, which also sell some hot meals to go! There is also a health food store nearby, street food, hip michelin-star restaurants and other hidden gems in this surging creative area. Around the house there are plenty of free parking spots for your car as well as the exits to the National freeways.

The historic, Art Deco and Bauhaus related building, with it’s elegant marble foyer and spacious apartments is located next to Kolonaki and Exarchia.

It was build in 1937 by the shipping magnate family Livanos for their own use.
The Penthouse Suite, the bar and the large Roof Garden with panoramic views of the Acropolis and Mount Lykabettos were constructed for celebrations, parties and to accommodate their guests.

The Acropolis line Metro station Panepistimio is only a five minutes walk.
neighborhood_overview:
The Penthouse Suite is located in the heart of Athens at the corner Asklipiou Street and Solonos.
The city areas Kolonaki and Exarcheia are bordering there.

The architectural "trilogy" Academy, University and the National Library designed in 1859 by the Danish architect Theophil Hansen is only 100 meters away. You can see their roofs from the terrace.

Kolonaki and Exarcheia with their many cafes, restaurants and bars are within a three minute walking distance.

The Parliament, Syntagma Square, the National Garden, the Numismatic Museum, the Old Parliament House, the Benaki Museum, Mount Lykabettus, and Omonia Square are about a 10 minute walk.

The Acropolis, the Acropolis Museum, Plaka, Monastiraki, the Temple of Olympian Zeus and the National Museum are within a 15 to 20 minute walking distance.

Syntagma square - Plaka - New Acropolis Museum 
 
Being on Syntagma square you can easily enter the area of Plaka which is the oldest and most prestigious neighbourhood of Athens. Don’t miss the chance to stroll around “Anafiotika” , a cosy district of Plaka that looks like a small island popped from the north slope of Acropolis. Plaka’s main pedestrian - only Kidathinaion and Adrianou you can find plenty of stores selling traditional goods, souvenirs, folk artifacts and Greek traditional food products. neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to Athens! Neapoli is a district rich in historic and modern culture, located on the northern slope of Lycabettus Hill. The name derives from the fact that it was the new city of Athens when it was starting to become urbanized in the mid 19th century.
It stretches between Lycabettus hill and Strefi Hill. Neapoli is the birthplace quarter of letters, arts, and culture! The neighborhood’s architecture has an identity with many neoclassical buildings and small urban squares with pine trees!

Retropolitan Laskareos is located in a central part of Athens, in the area of Neapolis! Despite its location, the tranquility and relaxation offered by the apartment make it unique. It is located very close to cafes, restaurants and supermarkets, offering immediate service to your needs!

• Acropolis (6.2 km)
• Acropolis Museum (3.2 km)

host_about:
Vaso‘s house is located in Ano Patissia, approximately 3 km from the center of Athens and in proximity to public transport stations (bus and metro).

Patissia is a historic district of Athens. At the end of the 19th and the beginning of the 20th century many wealthy Athenians chose this area to built their summer houses. For this reason one sees many neoclassical houses with the distinctive architecture of this period. These neoclassical summer houses with gardens consisted the first garden district of Athens, parts of which one can still recognize to date.

Vaso’s house is located in the center of this area (Kypriadou) which is situated very close to the Center but not inside the busy tourist area.

Patission street starts from the center of Athens (it is the extension of Aiolou street which leads to Acropole) and divides Patissia in two areas. Ano Patissia (Upper side Patissia), where Vaso’s house is located, retains many of the characteristic elements of the old Athens (houses with gardens, squares, green sides). Kato Patissia (Lower side Patissia) underwent a rapid urbanization during the 1950’s and today in some parts the effects of the economical crisis are quite evident.

Ano Patissia during the 1980’s and 1990’s was a reference point for the rock stage with many of the classical rock spots still in operation, very close to Vaso’s house.

Patission street is of historical significance for Greece’s contemporary political history. The Polytechnic school and the School of Economics are located on this street, the universities from which the riot against the dictatorship commenced (in 1973).

Vaso’ s house was originally one of these summer villas and was renovated in 1987. The ground floor is built from stone and thus particularly cool during the summer months! It retains many of the characteristics of the old architectural style, with tall ceilings, spacious rooms and a lemon tree garden.

Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

neighborhood_overview:
The Koukaki area, is Athens hippest neighborhood.

Just underneath the Acropolis lies one of the city's most creative and charming corners, nicknamed as Athens ‘Little Paris’.

Koukaki was named after Koukakis, a local bed manufacturer who owned a factory near the historic Sygrou Fix building – which is today home to the National Museum of Contemporary Art. Next to the historic area of Plaka, Koukaki is the closest and most organized district neighboring the Acropolis.

It continues to preserve the glory of its past thanks to the well-preserved and renovated neoclassical homes that represent the Athenian Modernism movement which thrived in the interwar period.
host_about: Part of the Modernism movement and Art Nouveau, The Koukaki Residence abounds in breath taking design elements that will definitely conquer your heart! From the monumental entrance, to the signature stairway which is a work of art of its own, all reflect the nobility of the Greek Bourgeois family who lived in this building at the beginning of the century. All the above encircle the Secret Garden in the middle, which is the Koukaki Residence's best kept secret.

name: Spacious family home, view of Acropolis!
description: A very spacious, renovated, family apartment that accommodates up to 6 people. Two large bedrooms (one with partial Acropolis view). Large living room with smart tv ( with free Netflix!) and sofa-bed. Airconditioned and wifi throughout the house as well as a fully equipped kitchen. neighborhood_overview:
Kerameikos is the new 'Soho' of Athens, with most major historical sites located within a 25-minute walking radius. It is safe, urban, and lively, full of
unique shops, authentic tavernas, cafes, art galleries and so far remains un-touristic. Strolling through Kerameikos in the daytime can also be deceptively low-key. During the day many Greeks go about their day, but at night the many local bars, taverns, and hotspots fill up with mainly an artistic crowd from the surrounding areas. There is a supermarket and deli just 100 meters from the house, with fresh and organic fruits and vegetables, which also sell some hot meals to go! There is also a health food store nearby, street food, hip Michelin-star restaurants, and other hidden gems in this surging creative area. Around the house, there are plenty of free parking spots for your car as well as exits to the National freeways.

neighborhood_overview:
Plaka is the “neighbourhood of Gods” with Acropolis above.
The oldest and most picturesque part of Athens, is the ideal location for any visitor.
Plaka is considered the area that developed around the ancient Agora of Athens and is the oldest district in Athens, as it has been continuously inhabited for around three thousand years. Thus, Plaka has a long history and has played an important part in Athenian life, with many famous people having walked along its streets, from Pericles and Alexander the Great to Lord Elgin and Lord Byron, while many well-known Greek writers, actors and artists have lived here, like Giorgos Seferis, Kostis Palamas and Melina Merkouri to name a few.
During 1884 a large part of Plaka burned down due to a fire, giving the opportunity for extensive archaeological work in the Roman Agora and Hadrian’s library, while excavations in the area have been conducted ever since.

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

description: The metro is just eight minutes from my place, taking you to the Acropolis, Monastiraki, Thissio, Syntagma square and virtually anywhere. I have always loved Koukaki, not just because it is one of the most popular neighbourhoods globally for airbnb but because it is vibrant, friendly, artistic and can cater to all tastes. host_about:
My friends always tell me that they wish they could stay in my place all the time because it makes them feel good and has positive vibes. I do have an optimistic outlook on life, and I also love treating people like royalty, so maybe my home shares some of my qualities. I work as a make-up artist, masseuse and podologist, so I like helping people relax and feel at home. I love meeting new people and interacting with different cultures. In my spare time, I am involved in animal rescue, and I have helped to shelter, feed and find homes for hundreds of stray dogs and cats over the past sixteen years. Many of them required veterinary care because they were abused, malnourished, or sick. 
I take my hosting duties very seriously because I understand that the few days a guest stays at my place may be the only time of the year they can relax and recharge their batteries. Αncient Greeks believed that filoxenia (hospitality) was a sacred duty because the gods disguised themselves as guests and visited them in order to test their kindness. The host and the guests were united with eternal bonds of friendship which their children inherited. This is how I interact with my guests, always taking time to pay attention to individual needs and questions they may have or advice they need to get around. I look forward to welcoming you with a bottle of Greek wine.

neighborhood_overview:
Athens is one of the safest cities in the world. What you need to look out for, as in any touristy city, is pickpocketing. This applies especially if you’re going to use the public transport.
Keep your bag in the front of you, not on your back, and always keep your hands on your wallet and cell phone. Separate your travel documents and your money. If you notice a sudden crowd when you’re getting on the bus or the metro, it could be a team of pickpockets – don’t let yourself get distracted. Letting others touch your luggage on public transport is also not recommended.
As for areas to avoid, you should stay out of Omonoia Square, Vathis Square, Kaniggos square and Sofokleous Street – all are hangouts for the homeless, beggars and drug addicts.

Right in the heart of the commercial triangle of Athens which is - as denoted by its name – the market place of Athens and not only as the Metropolis of Athens is within 2-minute walking from the apartment. The “vertices” of the triangle are the three main squares of the city: Omonoia, Syntagma and Monastiraki.
The commercial triangle was used by the old Athenians for their daily shopping of all goods. Varvakeios, the meat market, the fish market and the popular Ermou street- which is the main commercial road of Athens are located here. What everyone finds specifically interesting is that the area is mainly organized the old way: each street is “themed” for specific goods: in Vyssis str. you will find stores that sell doorknobs of every kind, in Praxitelous str. shops with lamps, in Karageorgi Servias shops with fabrics and in Agiou Markou shops with low budget clothes and shoes.

neighborhood_overview:
🌟 Top Attractions Nearby
The Acropolis & Parthenon – Just a short metro ride or a 20-minute walk, this world-famous hilltop ruin is Athens' crown jewel. Walk among temples, statues, and history that dates back over 2,000 years.

Monastiraki Square – One of the most photographed places in Athens, full of souvenir shops, cafes, and the legendary flea market. Great for strolling, snacking, and soaking up the atmosphere.

Plaka – Right beneath the Acropolis, this charming old neighborhood is full of colorful houses, bougainvillea-lined steps, and romantic tavernas. Perfect for an evening walk and Greek dinner.

Syntagma Square & the Changing of the Guard – Watch the ceremonial guards outside the Greek Parliament in full traditional uniform. It happens every hour, and it’s a must-see!

Ermou Street – The city’s main shopping street, connecting Syntagma to Monastiraki. Lined with international stores and local boutiques — ideal for fashion lovers.

name: Enjoy Athens from a funky studio near Acropolis!
description:
Conveniently located in the heart of historical Athens, this 2019 utterly reconstructed studio is in the premises of an iconic shoe-factory from the 70’s, that was converted into a serviced condo-building.

Being one of the most popular and liveliest districts in the centre of Athens, Pangrati, is a neighborhood favored by locals and tourists. Near the apartment, you can find shops, bars, coffee shops, restaurants, tavernas, street food shops and more.

From the apartment one has easy and quick access to historical areas, archeological sites and shopping districts (by metro, 1 stop to reach Syntagma Square).
Acropolis, Panathenaic Stadium (first stadium of modern Olympic games), Plaka (old town of Athens) and many more important and interesting sites are all in walking distance from the apartment.
In 12 min you can also reach Kolonaki's posh area with its numerous cafés, restaurants, night clubs and elegant shops.
Nearby you can also visit the Byzantine Museum, the Modern Art Gallery and the Benaki Museum among others.

It provides its guests with direct access to all MUST visit attractions. Bars and restaurants, subway, bus and train stops, as well as all the major sightseeings are within 3 minutes walking distance.

Constant WiFi and a fully equipped private kitchen are a few of the free offered amenities.
neighborhood_overview:
Psyri, a hip neighborhood, used to have in its premises the majority of the leather traders and craftsmen till the mid 80s’. Now, it has repositioned itself into a vibrant area full of stylish bars, traditional cafes and restaurants.

While walking during the daytime you can meet a variety of people, from businessmen to men selling and bargaining used stuff on the street.

Acropolis, the Acropolis museum, Plaka, Monastiraki flea market, as well as Syntagma square and all the upbeat Athens neighborhoods are in the immediate vicinity.

Upon arrival, we provide you with tailor-made recommendations. Enjoy “Athens by night” while being minutes from home ;)
host_about:
Kalimera (=Good Morning)! I am Alexandros, an ex-financier who turned into an entrepreneur.

I grew up in Athens, Greece, an awesome and vibrant city, where I studied Civil Engineering at NTUA. I was always keen on music, a passion which I flipped into DJing, yeap!!! Following my graduation I wanted to see the world and study abroad, so I attended Columbia University in NYC for my second Masters degree. The 2008 crash sent me directly to Germany where I started my career in banking.

After some years in corporate environments I decided to follow my real love, which is creating things from scratch, so I quit my job and alongside with my brother, George, we began a hospitality start-up.

We provide unique furnished apartments by offering personalized services!

It is so awesome to be an explorer and we believe that if you do not travel is like reading only the cover of the book. Hence,  t-r-a-v-e-l  :)

We hope to enjoy your staying with us!!!!

Keep it real,
Alexandros.

neighborhood_overview:
Keramikos (or Kerameikos) is named after Keramos, son of Dionysos and Ariadne, hero of the potters. Potters always lived in the area, in the banks of the Eridanos river that used to be here, along with the cemetery of ancient Athens.

Keramikos has always been an urban Athens neighborhood. Today you can find modern lofts and typical mid-war period houses, influenced by the modernist architecture of the 30s and the 50s and the Bauhaus school.
During the recent years Keramikos with the adjacent areas of Gazi and Metaxourgio has been transformed into the ‘hip’ area of Athens. description: Hello we are Florian and Nadja, we rent our little „house in house“ (that means separate entrance, own stairs (aka Mezzanine)The flat is located in downtown, more downtown is not possible. It is in a very quiet street, although it is situated in the heart of Exarchia, the famous alternative area for hanging and going out in Athens. The apartment is freshly renovated and we furnished it with a lot of love and details. We are happy to welcome you.
neighborhood_overview:
The district of Exarchia is famous for it´s open minded and left alternative residents.

A lot of artists, musicians and many social political engaged people live here. All revolutions in Greece have their beginning at the Platia Exarchia.
Athens is besides his ancient cultural heritage also pretty popular for his street art worldwide. Of course the graffiti scene of Athens has his origin in Exarchia.
Because of this colorful mix, the district became a magnet for night crawlers. And so you will find authentic Tavernas, good pubs, bars, live music and clubs.

Have in mind thus, you will not only find a positive inspiring vibe but also some homeless , drug addicted and begging people on the streets.
If you are more into the Kardashian way of life you might find yourself a bit overwhelmed at some point.
host_about: I am a Designer working and living in Athens and Munich, in fields of Interior Design, Installation, Graphic Design and fair settings. I love to travel and meet different people and new cultures, that´s why I am looking forward to welcome you in our flat.

This is a wonderful part of downtown Athens, offering proximity to some of the world’s most important landmarks, along with great options for dining and drinking, or meeting with business partners and friends.

Acropolis and the modern Acropolis Museum are found nearby, offering the opportunity to travelers to see from up close one of the most emblematic landmarks in the world. Kerameikos Ancient Cemetery and Ancient Agora, the Archaeological Museum and the National Library, Lycabettus and Syntagma Square, the Greek Parliament with the Changing of the Guards and the Temple of Olympian Zeus, these are just few of the attractions that can be reached within a few minutes from our apartments.

ANO PETRALONA, as featured in Monocle magazine’s video "Athens Favourite Neighbourhoods", is an excellent location for those who wish to live centrally, in a typically local neighborhood away from the tourist crowds.

The upcoming gentrification of historic hubs in central Athens (zone 1) particularly ANO PETRALONA, seemed the perfect location for seekers of a true urban experience. The area caters to locals, and lately we see an influx of young urbanites as well.

Despite elements of the occasional pothole and graffiti, ANO PETRALONA’s spirit of a bygone era with its traditional establishments and old-stone houses and pastel colors, is being revived by young creatives, global nomads, and travelers, who enjoy authentic culture. This is a friendly neighborhood, with all amenities nearby (supermarkets, organic store, hairdressers, dry-clean, baker, restaurants, etc.).

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

The upcoming gentrification of historic hubs in central Athens (zone 1) particularly ANO PETRALONA, seemed the perfect location for seekers of a true urban experience. The area caters to locals, and lately we see an influx of young urbanites as well.

Despite elements of the occasional pothole and graffiti, ANO PETRALONA’s spirit of a bygone era with its traditional establishments and old-stone houses and pastel colors, is being revived by young creatives, global nomads, and travelers, who enjoy authentic culture. This is a friendly neighborhood, with all amenities nearby (supermarkets, organic store, hairdressers, dry-clean, baker, restaurants, etc.).

Adjacent to Pagrati, an upcoming neighborhood with a vibrant nightlife, Kaisariani is surrounded by numerous restaurants, cafes and bars. The area’s trademark is Skopeftirio Grove, a 14-acre urban park painted with cobblestoned alleys, pine trees, firs and cypresses, ideal for a relaxing walk or an outdoor picnic. neighborhood_overview: Psyri is a gentrified Athens neighbourhood, today known for its restaurants, bars, live music tavernas, and small number of hotels. It's central square is called "Heroes square" (plateia Iroon), because the streets leading to it carry names of heroes of the Greek War of Independence (e.g. Karaiskakis, Miaoulis). In the era of the 'old Athens' (namely, during the last quarter of the 19th century), the nickname "plateia of Heroes" was a derisive reference to 'koutsavakides' (working class men), who would use it as a hangout.

The Ancient Agora of Athens, Stoa of Attalos, the Temple of Hephaestus and Kerameikos Archae-ological Museum can be entered from Thissio; all others, the National Observatory of Athens, Acropolis of Ath-ens, Philopappos Monument, Mouseion Hill, Pnyx, which is con-sidered the birthplace of Democracy, and the Mount Lycabet-tus can be easily reached or viewed from Thissio. A short stroll brings you to Patriarchou Ioakeim Street, a charming road lined with boutique shops, trendy bars, and cafes, leading to the lively Kolonaki Square. From there, key landmarks such as the National Garden, Monastiraki, Ermou Street, and even the Acropolis are all within walking distance.

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

description: My apartment is located on the 1st floor of a new and very well maintained residential building. Our block is in a very silent suburban neighborhood, close to the very center (8min ride to go downtown with the train). The train station of Kato Patissia (third line of metro, or else: green line) is just 8' walking distance and a very simple, easy route. The building itself is a super safe, family one, and the next door neighbors- Thanasis and Eftihia (same name as me!!!)- extremely friendly.
neighborhood_overview: The guests of Sweet & cozy suburban home may get lucky to experience and come across some old genuine Athenean moments one does not find in the very center anymore: the musician who plays acordeon and sings walking down the street- waiting for people to come out in their balconies and treat him with some money for his music, the watermelon merchant who drives through the streets and stops for you to purchase a juicy sweet watermelon (without having to carry it all the way from the super market!!!) if you yell at him from the balcony, the worker who passes through the neighborhood asking if someone needs emptying of their storage space, garage or getting rid of electrical devices/ furniture, etc.
host_about:
My name is Eftihia (Eftehea), from the words 'ef' and 'tihi' (tehe) which mean 'good' and 'luck' in ancient greek. My name is also a noun. In modern greek the word eftihia means happiness. For ancient greeks happy was the fortunate one. Nowdays happy is the joyful one. My name is quite a heavy thing to go by everyday, as it means something so great and simple (but veeeery complicated too..), that it is sometimes a real struggle to deliver its meaning and idea and project in in your life. And other's lives around you.

My parents origins are from the Peloponese and Zakynthos (Ionian Island). But I grew up in the wider terretory of Attica Prefecture, in particular in 2 suberbs of Athens- Marousi and Kifisia.

My profession is acting and as that started as a career (B.C. - before Crisis!!!) but has practically ended up a practical hobby (A.C.- after Crisis..), I am trying to reinvent myself and my life and scetch a 'plan B'..

Whatever that will occur to be, my true passion is walking barefoot on sharp rocks of isolated greek islands. If I was from India I think they would say I used to be a wild goat in a previous life. My technique in this strange extreme sport is really something to admire. I love walking in general, I like nature and even though I am definately a child of the city, my soul meets its 'core' when away from it. It is like the purity of my existence absolutely relates to the inviroment I find myself in. The landscape of a mountain or a beach or a lake or a river automatically turns me into a better person. My effort has always been to manage to carry that person with me even in the packed and trafficy Streets and Avenues of Athens.

My favourite time of the day in the area I leave in (where my house that welcomes airbnb guests is located) is between 2-6 in the morning. When the city sleeps one is able to 'pick up' and fully absorb this area's true energy. When crowded it is just another touristic place with great historical interest. But its healing effect one can only get when it is  q u i t e  and  p e a c e f u l.. At times of grief, pressure or distress I found that walking (AND jogging too!) around in that neighbourhood at these hours of the day was very therapeutic.

Sharing your house with people you don't know (and- at circummstances- you might actually never even meet!!!) became possible thanks to this whole airbnb notion that you created. It is a beautiful chain that connects people who wanted more- out of traveling- than a regular hotel or rudimantary furnished/equipped apartments. That chain allows travellers to make a 'subtour'  in their tour, experience how a person from a different country and culture lives. Like a quick whimsy eavesdropping or innocent peeping that might 'salt or sweeten up' the first and last moments of ones journey to a foreign place. 

So.. Long live the AirBnB!

Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

name: New Luxury Studio in the Heart of Thiseio.
description:
Located in the traditional neighbourhood of Thiseio, in the center of Athens, one of the most popular and historical places in Greece.
Renovated in 2021 this luxury apartment will provide you with everything you’ll need. The double bed will comfort you and recharge your batteries after a long day of exploring the beauties of Athens.
Just a few minutes away, in walking distance, you can find Thiseio Metro station and also, you visit all historical sites like Acropolis, Plaka and Monastiraki.
neighborhood_overview:
Every neighbourhood in Athens lucky enough to have a view of the Acropolis thinks that theirs is the best in the city. But you really can’t beat Thiseio to appreciate the majesty of the Parthenon. Walking up the footpath behind the Church of St. Marina and past the National Observatory of Athens up to Pnyx Hill (birthplace of democracy), where you’re greeted with a spectacular perspective on the entire ancient city.

While most views of Athens reveal a sun-bleached concrete jungle, from this tree-lined summit you see how the historical centre is really a green island. After a long day exploring the city, venturing up at sunset is a great way to unwind. If you ever grow tired of staring down on the Propylaea, the main entrance to the Acropolis, and the temple of Athena Nike, you can always turn around and look out towards the sea, Piraeus harbour, the ships coming to and from, and the islands that dot the horizon.

description: Our apartment is 91 sq meters and centrally located, 400 meters away from Panormou metro station that will get you within 10’ to Syntagma square, the Acropolis or Monastiraki. You can find on that day market stalls with fresh vegetables, fruits, and fish from all around Greece.

Historic urban neighbourhood, one of the last authentic and unspoiled in Europe. neighborhood_overview:
Everything is colorful, singular, painted in Exarcheia district of Athens. A popular district today, it is also the district of intellectuals, artists and many students, often leftists or anarchists and migrants.

This is also where most of Athens' printers, publishers, booksellers, record stores, internet cafes and organic grocery stores are located.

On Saturday mornings, the steep street of Kallidromiou turns into one of the most beautiful markets (laiki) in Athens, with piles of fresh fruits and vegetables from Greek producers, arranged under orange tarpaulins. The crowd is an odd mix of young and old Athenians, artists, migrants and celebrities.

The multicultural, audacious and politicized atmosphere of the neighborhood gives way to multiple spontaneous expressions in the streets. Urban spaces are covered with tags, scribbles, posters...but also a place of artistic expression that skillfully reflects the socio-political issues of the time.

Close to Thiseio and the Acropolis but safely removed from their tourist traps, Petralona blends old-school charm, artistic vibes and boho haunts. Like many parts of the downtown, this too, seems kind of disorganized and chaotic, with a haphazard mix of different architectural styles and lots of graffiti. But then again this is where its allure lays – in true Athenian style. Amid the whole scruffy setting there are alternative-chic joints – from traditional taverns with a twist, to experimental places featuring theater and gigs, Thai and French restaurants and trend-setting bars. Launched by a swarm of young creatives who’ve recently relocated in the area, these eye-catching spots are responsible for the area’s renaissance - Petralona is often dubbed the “New Gazi”. It still retains though a distinctly local character and feel, without being over-commercialized or pretentious like its fabled neighbor.

Petralona is also conveniently positioned for exploring the city on foot

host_about:
I am Giannis, an entrepreneur and a coffee shop owner. I really like meeting new people from all over the world while travelling or, even better, having them visit Athens and hosting them! I am energetic and forward-thinking (or so my friends and colleagues say about me), a physical as well as intellectual person. I enjoy football and alternative sports, but also reading good books and of course activities like puzzles and escape rooms, things I do for a living!
I have travelled all over Europe and Africa and I consider Paris and Budapest my favourite destinations, places of history but also modern and cosmopolitan, having many things to see and do.
Films and TV shows about historic events and murder mysteries are my favorite and recently I got infatuated with Money Heist (“La casa de Papel”). while my literature of choice is mainly classic and timeless. I could not imagine myself as I am today without having read “Around the World in 80 Days” in my childhood!
I enjoy Mediterranean and Greek traditional cuisine, but I would like to taste every culinary tradition the world has to offer.
As for a life moto? “You can learn more for a person by playing with him/her for an hour than by a year-long conversation”, by Greek philosopher Plato.

neighborhood_overview:
Close to Thiseio and the Acropolis but safely removed from their tourist traps, Petralona blends old-school charm, artistic vibes and boho haunts. Like many parts of the downtown, this too, seems kind of disorganized and chaotic, with a haphazard mix of different architectural styles and lots of graffiti. But then again this is where its allure lays – in true Athenian style. Amid the whole scruffy setting there are alternative-chic joints – from traditional taverns with a twist, to experimental places featuring theater and gigs, Thai and French restaurants and trend-setting bars.

Launched by a swarm of young creatives who’ve recently relocated in the area, these eye-catching spots are responsible for the area’s renaissance - Petralona is often dubbed the “New Gazi”. It still retains though a distinctly local character and feel, without being over-commercialized or pretentious like its fabled neighbor. Petralona is also conveniently positioned for exploring the city on foot

neighborhood_overview: Mets is a small neighborhood, a heartbeat from all the main touristic attractions of the city center(it is a 10 minutes walk from Acropolis and just 5 minutes from Kallimarmaro Stadium)but it is not touristic at all. It is located on Ardittos hill. A little bit of Montmartre, a little bit of East London, this is a place you should discover if you want to visit one of the most charming areas of Athens. Mets took its name from the beer house that was established on the hill in 1870 by the Bavarians who accompanied King Otto to Greece. In the 19th century, due to the area's proximity to the Palace and the city center, the neighborhood was populated by middle-class families who built elegant, big neoclassical houses and changed the character of the area completely. It is now considered one of the most stylish neighborhoods of the city. Many artists, musicians, actors, painters have moved in Mets and have given it a more bohemian character. neighborhood_overview:
Close to Thiseio and the Acropolis but safely removed from their tourist traps, Petralona blends old-school charm, artistic vibes and boho haunts. Like many parts of the downtown, this too, seems kind of disorganized and chaotic, with a haphazard mix of different architectural styles and lots of graffiti. But then again this is where its allure lays – in true Athenian style. Amid the whole scruffy setting there are alternative-chic joints – from traditional taverns with a twist, to experimental places featuring theater and gigs, Thai and French restaurants and trend-setting bars. Launched by a swarm of young creatives who’ve recently relocated in the area, these eye-catching spots are responsible for the area’s renaissance - Petralona is often dubbed the “New Gazi”.

It still retains though a distinctly local character and feel, without being over-commercialized or pretentious like its fabled neighbor. Petralona is also conveniently positioned for exploring the city on foot

neighborhood_overview:
Exarchia is one of Athens' oldest neighbourhoods, situated between the city's two main squares (Omonoia and Syntagma) and its biggest park, Pedion Areos. It is a place of great historical significance, as a lot of the country's modern history events have taken place in the area, the most famous one being the 1973 Polytechnic uprising against the military junta. It is also home to the National Archaeological Museum, a must-see for anyone interested in ancient Greece.
Due to its history, today Exarchia still remains a place popular with university students, artists, writers, etc, and many leftist organisations are based and operate in the area. Unfortunately, parts of the neighbourhood have also been used for drug-trafficking and drug use, but nowadays they have almost disappeared (from Exarchia, but not from downtown Athens in general).

Filopapou Hill, or Mousses Hill, or Segio hill, is a hill of Athens located across, southwest, from the Acropolis. Filopappou Hill is connected to the adjacent hills of the Observatory (Nymphs Hill) and Pnyx.

According to the ancient traveler Pausanias, the highest of the three hills west of the Acropolis, was named after the poet Moussaios, who lived, taught, and was buried in it. Lost in the natural rock square, at the northeast of the hill summit, with coaches to the west, that have a pound for statues, Thrania, and a bank for offers, it is believed that it belongs to the Tafikos Heron of Mousaios.

neighborhood_overview:
Ermou Street (Greek: Οδός Ερμού, Odos Ermou, "Hermes Street") is a one and a half kilometer-long road in central Athens, Greece, connecting Kerameikos archaeological site with the Syntagma Square through Monastiraki, Psiri and Thiseio.

neighborhood_overview:
Close to Thiseio and the Acropolis but safely removed from their tourist traps, Petralona blends old-school charm, artistic vibes and boho haunts. Like many parts of the downtown, this too, seems kind of disorganized and chaotic, with a haphazard mix of different architectural styles and lots of graffiti. But then again this is where its allure lays – in true Athenian style. Amid the whole scruffy setting there are alternative-chic joints – from traditional taverns with a twist, to experimental places featuring theater and gigs, Thai and French restaurants and trend-setting bars.

Launched by a swarm of young creatives who’ve recently relocated in the area, these eye-catching spots are responsible for the area’s renaissance - Petralona is often dubbed the “New Gazi”. It still retains though a distinctly local character and feel, without being over-commercialized or pretentious like its fabled neighbor. Petralona is also conveniently positioned for exploring the city on foot.

Hippy and modern bars, traditional and ethnic restaurants, cafes, brunch places, super markets, vegan choices, pizzerias, souvlaki's grills, grocery stores with fresh vegetables, traditional bakeries,a nd many more stores, are available all the time, just some meters from the apartment. host_about:
I am Giannis, an entrepreneur and a coffee shop owner. I really like meeting new people from all over the world while travelling or, even better, having them visit Athens and hosting them! I am energetic and forward-thinking (or so my friends and colleagues say about me), a physical as well as intellectual person. I enjoy football and alternative sports, but also reading good books and of course activities like puzzles and escape rooms, things I do for a living!
I have travelled all over Europe and Africa and I consider Paris and Budapest my favourite destinations, places of history but also modern and cosmopolitan, having many things to see and do.
Films and TV shows about historic events and murder mysteries are my favorite and recently I got infatuated with Money Heist (“La casa de Papel”). while my literature of choice is mainly classic and timeless. I could not imagine myself as I am today without having read “Around the World in 80 Days” in my childhood!

neighborhood_overview:
Neapoli is a vibrant, historic neighborhood in central Athens, part of the Exarchia area. Together with Exarchia, it forms a bohemian and lively area known for its collective and alternative culture, nightlife, and intellectual atmosphere.

It features a rich architecture with a mix of neoclassical buildings, and post-war apartments. There is a popular Saturday farmers' market at Kallidromiou Street, a main street in Neapoli with tavernas, bars, and groceries. You can find many underground bars, live music venues, and cozy cafés that stay open late throughout the small streets. As it is very close to the University of Athens and the Polytechnic School, it attracts students, artists, and activists. The streets are filled with colorful murals, graffiti.

Neapoli and Exarchia are raw, energetic, and unpolished neighborhoods, beloved by those who appreciate local life and a non-touristy side of Athens. Neapoli has a slightly more residential but still alternative feel.
