name: Zeus - Luxenia Suites
description: Nestled in the heart of Plaka, Athens, this charming apartment offers a serene retreat on a picturesque, quiet street. Blending traditional Greek charm with modern comforts, it features cozy interiors, elegant decor, and abundant natural light. The apartment boasts a well-equipped kitchen, a comfortable living area, and a private balcony with views of Plaka's historic district. Steps away from quaint cafes, local shops, and iconic landmarks, it’s a perfect haven for relaxation and exploration.
neighborhood_overview: Plaka is a district in the center of Athens below the Acropolis. It borders to the south with the district of Makrigianni, to the east with the area of the Temple of Olympian Zeus and Zappeion, to the north with the commercial center of Athens and to the west with Monastiraki. It has been characterized as a traditional settlement. Plaka is one of the few districts of the city -if not the only one- which has been continuously inhabited since antiquity and was, among other things, the center of Ancient Athens. The direct connection of the area with the glorious past of Ancient Athens, which becomes obvious to the visitor from the dozens of monuments scattered in it have made it known -and not unfairly- as the "Quarter of the Gods".

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

The spirit of community and simplicity remains, with a concomitant style of the unadorned.
Young creative Athenians have banded together to open alternative businesses such as social-conscious cafés to old-style tsipouradika (spots mainly serving tsipouro spirit accompanied by small dishes) with a modern twist. neighborhood_overview:
The flat is located behind the Kalimarmaro, also known as the Panathenaic Stadium, is a historic stadium located in Athens, Greece. It is one of the most significant landmarks of Athens and holds great cultural and historical importance.

The stadium was originally built in the 4th century BCE and was used for the Panathenaic Games, which were athletic competitions held in ancient Greece as part of the Panathenaic festival. The stadium was reconstructed in marble in 144 CE by Herodes Atticus, a wealthy Athenian Roman senator, and it is this structure that remains today.

The Kalimarmaro is a remarkable architectural achievement, as it is entirely built of marble. It has a horseshoe shape and can seat approximately 50,000 spectators. The track is made of clay and measures 204.07 meters in length, which is the standard length for modern Olympic Games.

neighborhood_overview:
Kerameikos, located in Athens, Greece, is an ancient and historic neighborhood with a rich cultural and archaeological significance. Named after the ancient cemetery that once occupied the area, Kerameikos offers a captivating blend of ancient ruins, modern attractions, and a vibrant local atmosphere.

One of the major highlights of Kerameikos is its archaeological site, which holds great historical importance. Visitors can explore the well-preserved remnants of tombs, burial mounds, and the ancient city walls, providing a fascinating glimpse into Athens' past.

Adjacent to the archaeological site is the Kerameikos Museum, which houses a vast collection of ancient artifacts discovered in the area. The museum offers a comprehensive overview of the burial customs, artwork, and daily life of the ancient Athenians. Visitors can admire intricate pottery, sculptures, and other archaeological finds that provide insight into the city's rich history.

name: Casa Mushidora: Art Retro Chic Hidden Gem
description: Sustainable architecture from the past with Garden. Stone built in 1936, the Ground-Level served for a long time as Summer-Lodge, Cellar and Auxiliary space. We found it neglected, but its preserved materials and atmosphere, inspired us to dedicate nearly 5 years to restore it with modern twists (down to its infrastructure) and turn it into a small urban oasis, introvert and quiet, ideal for relaxation and sleep, study or meditation. The apartment uses the SW part of a private Courtyard.
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment consists of a bedroom, dining room, living room, kitchen, bathroom, a laundry-storage room, and is equipped with central heating (gas), air-condition, ventilation, Wi-Fi, two TV sets, authentic furniture and unique objects.

In the back, with dual access from living room and kitchen, there is a luminous, paved courtyard and garden, with a tall palm tree, sounds and impressions of bygone times.

The building is among other landmarks around Amerikis Square, a few steps from Lela Karagianni's restored house. Within a 5-minute walk there are supermarkets, parkings, petrol stations, banks, post office, pharmacies, as well as café restaurants and bars.
host_about: We moved in the area when our son was 2 y/o. From the start I've appreciated its surprising joyfulness, safety, multi-ethnicity, proximity to the city center... This positivity inspired me to dare and acquire our home 4 years later, just before the pandemic. I feel outrageously privileged and thankful for it! Love and not reason led us to painstakingly renovate-revive the ground level and garden, abandoned since the 70s, and we're proud!

Psirri (also spelled Psiri or Psyrri) is a lively and historic neighborhood in central Athens, known for its unique blend of tradition and modern flair.
Once home to leather workshops, candle makers, and other artisans, Psirri still hosts some traditional crafts alongside a vibrant mix of tavernas, bars, and contemporary eateries. Its streets are also famous for bold street art and neoclassical charm.

Ideally located just minutes from Monastiraki metro station—with direct links to Athens Airport and Piraeus Port—Psirri sits right next to Plaka, making it a perfect base for exploring the city.

neighborhood_overview:
Thissio is one of Athens’ most scenic and culturally rich neighborhoods—an area where ancient ruins, leafy promenades, and cozy cafés come together under the Acropolis.

🌿 What to Do & See in Thissio:
1. Stroll Along Apostolou Pavlou Street
This beautiful pedestrian street is the heart of Thissio. Lined with cafés, street musicians, and local artists, it offers stunning views of the Acropolis as you walk toward the historic center.

2. Visit the Temple of Hephaestus

neighborhood_overview:
Ano Petralona originates from the Greek words of "Petra" (stone) and "Aloni" (threshing floor), since they were used to thresh grain before urbanisation. It is one of the most historical areas of Athens, where old traditional houses are located since the Asia Minor immigration. Even Dimofontos st, has its own historical significance, as it originates from ancient Greek figure of Dimofontas, son of Theseus, who fought in the Trojan war.

The area is the epitomy of the center as it's walking distance from Gkazi, Thiseio, Acropolis and also the Metro station. Thus, it combines all desires of entertainment, from party to cultural-related to local hangouts for people wanting to take a glimpse of the Greek lifestyle. neighborhood_overview: Living Stone Pearl is located in Psyri, the artistic, vibrant & bohemian neighborhood in the heart of Athens, below the shadow of the Acropolis. It is reached easily by the central and iconic “Monastiraki” Metro station or the Athens Railway “Thissio” station. The area around it, the Historic Centre of Athens, is the literal heart of the city’s rich nightlife, while also being exceptionally close to all major landmarks of the Greek capital.
host_about:
I am Giannis, an entrepreneur and a coffee shop owner. I really like meeting new people from all over the world while travelling or, even better, having them visit Athens and hosting them! I am energetic and forward-thinking (or so my friends and colleagues say about me), a physical as well as intellectual person. I enjoy football and alternative sports, but also reading good books and of course activities like puzzles and escape rooms, things I do for a living!
I have travelled all over Europe and Africa and I consider Paris and Budapest my favourite destinations, places of history but also modern and cosmopolitan, having many things to see and do.
Films and TV shows about historic events and murder mysteries are my favorite and recently I got infatuated with Money Heist (“La casa de Papel”). while my literature of choice is mainly classic and timeless. I could not imagine myself as I am today without having read “Around the World in 80 Days” in my childhood!
I enjoy Mediterranean and Greek traditional cuisine, but I would like to taste every culinary tradition the world has to offer.
As for a life moto? “You can learn more for a person by playing with him/her for an hour than by a year-long conversation”, by Greek philosopher Plato.

It is located in the center of Athens while at the same time maintaining the elements of the neighborhood and this is the main contrast that characterizes it. It is one of the areas that when you walk through its streets you look up. Not so much because apartment buildings have some special beauty, but because there is "life" there. Behind the colored awnings, in the conversations that can be heard from the open windows, in the spread clothes that add extra color to the balconies. It has several squares and gathering places that gives it vitality.

It is close to the Athens University of Economics and Business and is bordered by Pedion Areos, which is the largest public park in Athens with the Alsos theatre within. neighborhood_overview:
One of the least touristic yet wonderful areas of Athens with many things to offer. Pagrati/Mets is full of hip bars and cafés from high-end Michelin star dining (Spondi) to more casual joints (Fish Point) with it’s half fish market/ half sushi offerings. Make sure to stop by the organic grocery next door!

Just minutes from Alsos Park where you can find a perfect afternoon walk in the wooded pine tree grounds. This area is situated just behind the Panathenaico stadium and at the far end it meets the First Cemetery of Athens. Go there for a peaceful round and visit many 19th century graves.

At the center is Varnava square, a bustling circle with many cafe's and hip corner bars. Traditional food, meze (small plate) dinner options and late night crawls can all be found. This is an exciting area with the new Goulandris Museum of Modern Art just 5 minutes away by foot.

Koukaki holds a special place among Athens’ inner-city neighborhoods. Wedged between the ancient glory of the Acropolis hill and the rumbling traffic of Syngrou Avenue, it’s a district of intriguing contradictions. As one of the most rapidly evolving pockets of central Athens, cool Koukaki combines intimacy with authenticity.

Kolonaki is full of parks and gardens and is defined by its classical and modernist buildings which make it one of the most exquisite neighborhoods in Athens. This is a charming district to discover by foot and a great place to enjoy a beverage or a bite to eat in any of its modern terraces and restaurants. It is also renowned for its shopping streets packed with high-end boutiques, fashionable clothing stores, and where the top Greek designers sell their products. Last but not least, Kolonaki is home to the Presidential Palace, the Maximos Mansion, the Parliament, many Embassies and Ministries and is the safest disctrict in Athens.

Victoria Neighbourhood is one of the oldest in downtown Athens. It got its name from the homonym Square, in the heart of the neighborhood. The Square was named after Queen Victoria, in her honor, the year 1864. The area is home to one of Greece’s oldest universities in the shape of the Athens Polytechnic, cultural venues from museums to record stores, and great food and drink.

The start of construction on a new metro station in the central square last year marked a turning point in the area, with many fearing that the spirit of the neighbourhood will be eradicated.

neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located near Victorias Square. Around the square, the homonymous district has been developed. Since the 1940s the district has been one of Athens' best and most sought after, comparable to Kolonaki. On its streets there are important examples of classical modernism, such as the Spathari block (Mavrommatia street), the Sarantopoulos block (27 Derigni street), as well as the buildings on Heiden 1 and 2. The luxurious apartments of these buildings were addressed to the bourgeoisie of Athens at the time, since they provided a variety of amenities and had high quality architectural elements.

Gradually, the area began to severely decline, largely due to its abandonment by its original inhabitants. Since the worst days, there has been an improvement in the neighborhood around the square, which is linked to the general upgrading of downtown Athens. Nowadays, during the weekdays, the area is dominated by the students of the Athens University of Economics and Business

TopHouzzing’s story is simple yet exciting! We are Maria & Alex, the founders, both engineers. So we were already working together in the design & construction sector, so we  dealt with properties all the time. We are both into details, both love doing something right from scratch.

While we were traveling to new places and meeting old friends / making new ones, we felt what a rental should feel like, what it should offer guests like ourselves. Lots were missing, especially the simple little things that makes a visitor feel right at home -away from home. We then decided to start a rentals & real estate management company. It was July 2015 and we named it TopHouzzing Properties - the mission was simply to offer truly top accommodation to our guests. Starting then with a couple of our own properties, refurbished completely, we embarked on a great journey. 

Today the company manages close to 100 properties and growing steadily, mostly in Athens but also in mainland Greece and islands, flats, villas and so on. TopHouzzing  also offers consulting & real estate, design & construction and other professional services in its portfolio.

Hard work and our passion paid off. Our success is clearly stated not only in the many owners that trust us with their properties but even more in the hundreds 5-star reviews from guests from all over the world,  leading us to have a record of 14 consecutive quarters-since the company’s inception- SuperHost status on Airbnb!

name: Apartment in Panathenaic Stadium
description:
Our cozy and beautifully renovated one bedroom apartment, is situated in the vibrant and historic neighborhood of the Panathenaic/ Kallimarmaro area in central Athens. It will cater for your needs while working or exploring the beautiful attractions which are conveniently located within walking distance from the apartment.

The apartment is surrounded by most means of transportation, trolleys, buses, the tram,as well as the Syntagma, Evangelismos and Acropolis metro stations.
neighborhood_overview:
It is ideally just a minute walk from the Panathenaic Stadium, where the modern Olympic games took place, a 5 minute walk to the temple of Zeus, you can also leisurely walk through the Zappion/ the National Garden which can lead you to the Parliament and to the center of the robust and vibrant Syntagma square where all the shops, boutiques, cafes and bistros create a wonderful color and character, all within a 15 minute walk.

The ancient town of Plaka is also within walking distance, which can take you back in time while strolling on the paved streets with shops and  amazing restaurants and taverns where you can enjoy delicious international and local cuisine.

The National Gallery, devoted to Greek and European art from the 14th century to 20th century, The Museum of Modern Art, The Goulandris Museum of Contemporary Art, which houses exquisite displays of famous artists,  are among the most important attractions within walking distance from the apartment.

This is a quiet residential area of Athens that offers proximity to some of the most important landmarks in the world, as well as various restaurants, bakeries and stores. The emblematic Acropolis is a short 10-minute stroll away and so is the hill of Filopapou. With the nearest central metro station (Acropolis) at 500 metres, public transport connections – both bus and tube - are excellent, if you want to venture beyond the limits of the city centre, every corner of which, is accessible by foot.
Kallimarmaron, the only stadium in the world made entirely from marble is 800 away.

host_about:
I am from Athens, however I have very close ties with two beautiful Greek islands Santorini and Patmos.

As my father’s family is from Santorini I spent all my summers there. Since I am a licensed tour guide, in 2004 I decided to move to Santorini in order to work there. This was a great chance to start renovating my family’s properties in order to be able to share them with people from all over the world. 

In addition, many years ago, my mother visited the island of Patmos, fell in love with it and decided to buy two beautiful pieces of land, including very old farmhouses in ruinous condition, that she slowly renovated. In this way, our family and numerous friends enjoyed many unforgettable Patmos Easters and summers. Nowadays, I am responsible for the good condition of the houses that I rent out and share the beauty and special ambiance of this island with our guests.

I am very lucky since my twin daughters, Alexandra and Christina, having completed their studies abroad in hospitality management and tourism, returned to their roots in order to continue and develop what I started.  Genuine hospitality, love and respect for the island, as well as the embracement of the local culture define our core values. Nowadays we all share our time between Santorini, Patmos and Athens, and have the honor and pleasure to share our family’s story and our love for these islands, with visitors from all over the world. 

After many years in the hospitality industry, today I have the pleasure along with my daughters to embrace one more much loved island home, my husband's summer house on the island of Hydra. The house was built by my father in law 40 years ago. My husband Dimitris will be managing the house in Hydra.

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

neighborhood_overview:
Syntagma, located at the very heart of Athens, is a neighborhood that beautifully encapsulates the essence of the city, blending historical significance with modern vibrancy. Here’s an overall look at what makes Syntagma a prime destination for visitors.

Ermou Street, starting at Syntagma Square, is a shopper’s paradise with a mix of luxury boutiques and popular retail chains. The area is also known for its diverse dining options, from traditional Greek tavernas to chic international restaurants and cafes.

The National Garden, adjacent to the square, provides a lush retreat with walking paths and serene spots. The nearby Zappeion Hall and garden offer additional green spaces and host cultural events.

Syntagma is the perfect base in Athens, offering rich history, cultural attractions, excellent shopping and dining, beautiful parks, and a lively nightlife. Its central location and vibrant atmosphere make it ideal for both short visits and extended stays

neighborhood_overview:
The Athens National Garden

The Athens National Garden, originally the Royal Garden, is a verdant oasis bursting with history and biodiversity in the heart of Athens, right next to the Greek Parliament.

This enchanting sanctuary was commissioned by Queen Amalia in 1838 and designed by the visionary agronomist Friedrich Schmidt. Spanning about 15.5 hectares (38 acres), the garden is a living museum, showcasing over 500 plant species from around the world, including towering Washingtonia palms, exotic Canary Island date palms, and Chinese hibiscus.

Stepping into the garden is like traveling through time. Wander through its pathways and you’ll encounter ancient Roman ruins such as a Roman villa adorned with intricate mosaics, imposing columns, and remnants of ancient Roman baths.

A striking marble inscription commissioned by Roman Legion officer Laius Aettius, celebrating victories over Germanic tribes, adds a touch of historical gravitas.

I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

neighborhood_overview: Kynosargous is a historic neighborhood in Athens, Greece, known for its rich cultural heritage and archaeological significance. Located southeast of the Acropolis, this area was historically associated with the ancient gymnasium of Cynosarges, a site where athletes trained and philosophers like Antisthenes, the founder of Cynicism, taught. The neighborhood's name, meaning "white dog" in Greek, is rooted in local mythology. Today, Kynosargous blends its ancient past with modern urban life, featuring a mix of residential buildings, shops, and cafes. Its proximity to key landmarks, such as the National Museum of Contemporary Art and the Ilisos River, makes it a vibrant and historically layered district within the bustling city of Athens.

Explore the Plaka Neighborhood: Athens' Historical Heart

Nestled at the foot of the ancient Acropolis, the Plaka neighborhood is a captivating blend of history, culture, and modernity. It's a place where the past and present coexist, offering visitors an unparalleled experience of Athens' rich heritage. Dominating the skyline, the Acropolis is a symbol of classical civilization, featuring iconic structures like the Parthenon, the Erechtheion, and the Temple of Athena Nike. Stroll through the remnants of the Ancient Agora, once the heart of Athenian democracy, where philosophers like Socrates and Plato once walked.

The neighborhood is home to several world-class museums, including the Acropolis Museum, which houses priceless artifacts and offers a direct view of the Acropolis through its glass walls. Staying here places you within walking distance of Athens' most iconic landmarks. The Acropolis and its new museum are just a short stroll away, offering a glimpse into ancient Greek civilization. Syntagma Square, the city's central hub, is also nearby, providing easy access to public transportation and the ceremonial changing of the guard at the Hellenic Parliament.

In the evenings, Plaka comes alive with music and dining, offering an authentic Athenian experience. The neighborhood's unique blend of history and modernity makes it a captivating area to explore and enjoy.

Exarchia is one of Athens’ most vibrant and alternative neighborhoods, known for its artistic atmosphere, rebellious spirit, and deep cultural history. Located near the city center, it offers a unique mix of historical sites, street art, cozy cafés, and a lively nightlife scene. One of its biggest highlights is Lycabettus Hill, which offers the most breathtaking panoramic view of Athens.

Must-Visit Places in Exarchia

1. Lycabettus Hill (Lofos Lykavittou)

Standing at 277 meters, Lycabettus Hill is the highest point in central Athens and offers unmatched panoramic views of the Acropolis, the Aegean Sea, and the cityscape. Visitors can reach the top by hiking through pine-covered trails or taking the funicular railway. At the summit, the Chapel of St. George, an open-air theater, and a café provide the perfect setting to enjoy the scenery, especially at sunset.

neighborhood_overview:
Main Attractions in the area:

- Strefi Hill, despite its small extent it constitutes a green oasis in the centre of the city. Here you can find sport facilities and a summer stone theatre, while from the top you have panoramic view of the city.

- Lycabetus Theater. This open-air theatre was built in the period of 1964-65 by architect T. Zenetos on the ruins of an old quarry.

- Patission street, a busy street with interesting buildings, amongst which are the Neoclassical mansions of the Polytechnic School and the National Archaeological Museum, which ranks among the leading museums in the world and hosts rare art treasures from the Neolithic era up to the Roman period.

- Exarchia area, a charming and very lively neighborhood, traditional a meeting point and home to many students and artists. From Exarcheia, crossing the Neapoli neighborhood, you can climb the verdant Lycavittos Hill. From its top you have a view of the entire city, all the way

host_about:
I am Giannis, an entrepreneur and a coffee shop owner. I really like meeting new people from all over the world while travelling or, even better, having them visit Athens and hosting them! I am energetic and forward-thinking (or so my friends and colleagues say about me), a physical as well as intellectual person. I enjoy football and alternative sports, but also reading good books and of course activities like puzzles and escape rooms, things I do for a living!
I have travelled all over Europe and Africa and I consider Paris and Budapest my favourite destinations, places of history but also modern and cosmopolitan, having many things to see and do.
Films and TV shows about historic events and murder mysteries are my favorite and recently I got infatuated with Money Heist (“La casa de Papel”). while my literature of choice is mainly classic and timeless. I could not imagine myself as I am today without having read “Around the World in 80 Days” in my childhood!
I enjoy Mediterranean and Greek traditional cuisine, but I would like to taste every culinary tradition the world has to offer.
As for a life moto? “You can learn more for a person by playing with him/her for an hour than by a year-long conversation”, by Greek philosopher Plato.

Starting then with a couple of our own properties, refurbished completely, we embarked on a great journey. 

Today the company manages close to 100 properties and growing steadily, mostly in Athens but also in mainland Greece and islands, flats, villas and so on. TopHouzzing  also offers consulting & real estate, design & construction and other professional services in its portfolio.

Hard work and our passion paid off. Our success is clearly stated not only in the many owners that trust us with their properties but even more in the hundreds 5-star reviews from guests from all over the world,  leading us to have a record of 14 consecutive quarters-since the company’s inception- SuperHost status on Airbnb!

We take very good care of our guests and so do we with owners. You see, we both think as guests & owners ourselves. We are waiting anxiously to host you or to manage your property, in both cases you are in good hands with us.

Hi everyone. I am Stratos Zafeiriadis

I am a husband, a father of a 3yrs old child, a host, an Airbnb Community Leader in the capital of Greece, an Experience maker and a property manager in Greece (“where else” lol). 

I love Greece, its outstanding beauty and I have a dream:  to transmit to all my guests the hidden charm and all the secrets of my beloved country starting from A to Z. That’s why i am established from Athens to Zakynthos

During the summer I move to Zakynthos and here I like to express all my devotion for my island. I have created the Zante Free Walking Tour in order to widespread the beauty and history of my place. I really love this activity and I look forward to show it to you in one of the most beautiful places in the world! I’m not here to propose you just a nice accommodation. 

I always try to make your trip a lifetime memory. That’s why I could advise you places (secret or not) you will never been, places you will never imagine that exist! 

In Zakynthos also I run our family properties Alta Mare Villa Zakynthos and Alta Mare City View Luxury Apt (our new project).

During winter I move to Athens where I am proud to be the Airbnb Community Leader of Athens and Attica Region.

I’d love to answer your questions and share with you my favorite spots of Athens and Zakynthos, the places where I actually live and love 

Stratos Zafeiriadis

description:

host_about:
I am Giannis, an entrepreneur and a coffee shop owner. I really like meeting new people from all over the world while travelling or, even better, having them visit Athens and hosting them! I am energetic and forward-thinking (or so my friends and colleagues say about me), a physical as well as intellectual person. I enjoy football and alternative sports, but also reading good books and of course activities like puzzles and escape rooms, things I do for a living!
I have travelled all over Europe and Africa and I consider Paris and Budapest my favourite destinations, places of history but also modern and cosmopolitan, having many things to see and do.
Films and TV shows about historic events and murder mysteries are my favorite and recently I got infatuated with Money Heist (“La casa de Papel”). while my literature of choice is mainly classic and timeless. I could not imagine myself as I am today without having read “Around the World in 80 Days” in my childhood!

neighborhood_overview:
Koukaki is one of the oldest neighborhoods of Athens and owes its name to Koukakis Georgios who had a large bed factory, that operated pre-war in Sigrou street, close to the FIX beer factory (now the National Museum of Modern Art).
Koukaki is located on the south side of the Philopappou Hill. It borders Petralona, Kallithea, Neos Kosmos, Acropolis, Plaka and Singrou Avenue.
It is a densely built area, saturated already since the 1960s and 1970s. It is, however, a quite expensive district due to its location, as it is located beneath the Acropolis and the Philopappou Hill and very close to the historical center of Athens. It is also a lively, charming area with many shopping and entertainment opportunities and good public transportation: Two metro stations "Sigrou-Fix” and "Acropolis", tram, yellow bus line 1,5 and 15, bus to the cape Sounion, Piraeus port and all lines to the Athenian riviera.
Recently, Koukaki has become very popular to young people and visitors.

See you soon!

This area is one of Athens’ most vibrant and diverse districts, offering a mix of urban character, cultural landmarks, and authentic local experiences.

Omonoia Square is a major transport hub, connecting you effortlessly to the rest of the city via metro, suburban trains, buses, and trams. From here, you can reach popular destinations like Monastiraki, Syntagma, Plaka, and the Acropolis within minutes. The metro also provides a direct connection to both the port of Piraeus and the Athens International Airport.

For students and remote workers, the area offers convenience and accessibility. You’ll find universities, study-friendly cafés, bookstores, and co-working spaces nearby. Daily essentials are easy to access too, with supermarkets, pharmacies, bakeries, and local markets just around the corner.

neighborhood_overview:
Plaka is a charming and historic neighborhood located in the heart of Athens, Greece. It is considered one of the oldest neighborhoods in Athens, with its roots dating back to the ancient Greek and Roman eras. Plaka is located just beneath the Acropolis, which makes it one of the most popular tourist destinations in Athens.

The narrow streets of Plaka are lined with colorful neoclassical buildings, small shops, restaurants, cafes, and bars. The architecture of the buildings reflects the rich history of the area, with a mix of Greek, Ottoman, and neoclassical styles.

Plaka is known for its lively atmosphere and vibrant nightlife. In the evenings, the area comes alive with street musicians, performers, and people enjoying the warm Mediterranean weather. There are also plenty of rooftop bars and restaurants where you can enjoy a drink or a meal while taking in stunning views of the Acropolis.

One of the main attractions of Plaka is its archaeological sites

neighborhood_overview:
The area:

Situated in the prestigious neighborhood of Kolonaki, this area represents one of Athens’ most refined and cosmopolitan quarters, ideal for travelers seeking both elegance and proximity to cultural landmarks. Kolonaki is synonymous with sophistication: its tree-lined streets are home to high-end boutiques, art galleries, wine bars, and gourmet restaurants, while its stylish cafés are perfect for people-watching, as Athenians and visitors alike gather in Kolonaki Square, the district’s lively heart. Just a short walk away lies Mount Lycabettus, the city’s highest hill, where visitors can hike or take the funicular to enjoy breathtaking views of Athens and the Aegean. The neighborhood also offers cultural highlights such as the Museum of Cycladic Art, the Benaki Museum, and the Byzantine & Christian Museum, all within easy reach. Despite its upscale character, the area retains a welcoming local feel, with traditional tavernas tucked alongside luxury venues.
